saw.short: Bradley Walsh's Channel 4 quiz wasn't what it seemed
saw.headline: Bradley Walsh's Channel 4 quiz *wasn't what it seemed*
saw.what: Sunday's “The Million Pound Shot” was staged: the contestants and a heckler were actors, and the studio audience didn't know. Walsh told them: “Everything you've seen tonight draws on the techniques used by the gambling industry to manipulate its customers.” Viewers were pointed to the National Gambling Helpline, 0808 8020 133.
saw.why: A week of “is it a hoax?” guessing became the show's point. Keep gambling jokes out of posts.

saw.short: Celebrity Traitors' finale dominates social media
saw.headline: Celebrity Traitors' finale *dominates social media*
saw.what: The 80-minute finale on Friday night “dominated social media”, per The Poke, which rounded up 23 of the funniest reaction posts. The BBC reports an 11.2m average overnight audience, with a peak of 11.6m, a series high.
saw.why: Fans turned the finale into a live group chat, and the viewing figures backed it up.
saw.source: The Poke, 30 Oct; Irish News (PA), 31 Oct

saw.short: Maya Jama's Mo Farah costume wins Halloween
saw.headline: Maya Jama's *Mo Farah costume* wins Halloween
saw.what: Maya Jama posted a Halloween look as Mo Farah on Instagram: bald cap, facial hair, sports kit and a necklace, doing the Mobot pose with medals he gave her. Metro says she was declared “winner” of Halloween. Farah said on FaceTime: “I swear down, I thought that was me for a second!”
saw.why: Full commitment plus one real prop beats a half-hearted costume.

saw.short: Strictly's presenter is mocked for skipping Halloween costume
saw.headline: Strictly's *no-costume suit* gets spotted on Halloween week
saw.what: On Saturday viewers mocked presenter Josh Widdicombe for wearing a plain green suit while others dressed up: “Why is Josh the only one who isn't dressed up?” On Sunday the show held its first-ever three-couple dance-off.
saw.why: Viewers watch with a phone in hand, and a low-effort moment becomes the joke.

saw.short: Fallon Sherrock's Netflix darts challenge sparks a backlash
saw.headline: Fallon Sherrock's *Netflix darts challenge* sparks a backlash
saw.what: Netflix's “Beat Luke Littler”, hosted by Gary Lineker, aired on Friday. Some fans criticised Fallon Sherrock's inclusion because she has no PDC Tour Card; she replied: “I'm just so happy to overcome all the hate and win.” Metro and LADbible report she won £501,000 in a single 501 leg.
saw.why: A big prize and an underdog gave people strong views. The reply did the work.

saw.short: Argos's Christmas ad casts Richard Ayoade as Scrooge
saw.headline: Argos's Christmas ad *casts Richard Ayoade as Scrooge*
saw.what: Argos's “Tales of Argos Past” spoofs A Christmas Carol, with Richard Ayoade as Scrooge and two toy “ghosts”, Connie and Trevor, helping him choose a present for his mum. Metro says Argos, Sainsbury's, Tesco and Debenhams are among the UK brands that have launched, and John Lewis hasn't yet.
saw.why: UK Christmas ad season has started. Christmas Carol spoofs are everywhere: Walmart's Muppets ad last week, now Argos.

platform.short: Threads tests “Threads Friends”, a 50-person close-friends list
platform.headline: Threads tests *“Threads Friends”*, a close-friends list
platform.what: Threads is testing a list of up to 50 people for posts only they see. Members are told they're on your list, and likes and replies from list members are visible to others on it. The test is in Ireland, Italy and Japan, though anyone worldwide can be added.
platform.why: Smaller-circle posting comes to Threads. It's not in the UK test yet.

platform.short: YouTube tests a 30-day self-correct period for spam strikes
platform.headline: YouTube tests a *30-day self-correct period* for spam strikes
platform.what: YouTube is testing a change for channels that reach three strikes in 90 days. Instead of termination, eligible channels enter a 30-day locked period: they can't upload or comment, but can edit or delete the violating videos, or appeal. It says this is early testing.
platform.why: A second chance for creators and brand channels hit by spam strikes. Keep channel access and strikes under review.
